cards.method: Unit-root & normality prechecks (ADF/KPSS/PP/Jarque-Bera)
cards.when: a fast standardised first look at the stationarity of a univariate series + residual normality; ready-made p-values
cards.when_not: you need the test regression/DF-GLS/break-aware (-> #2); seasonal (-> #89); structural break; panel (-> #6)

alternatives.criterion: DF-GLS/explicit critical values/Zivot-Andrews break-aware

alternatives.alt: ADF+KPSS confirmatory (both nodes are on this card)
alternatives.criterion: established practice: opposite H0, cross-check for I(1)
the non-stationarity may be seasonal

output_key_fields: statistic: value of the statistic; p_value: ready-made p-value (the main decision)
lag_order/truncation_lag: lag k (ADF) or truncation lag; df: 2 (JB)
decision: pre-computed interpretation at alpha
warnings: 'p-value smaller/greater than printed' -> p-value clamped (0.01/0.10), not exact
interpretation_traps: KPSS polarity: H0=stationarity -> rejection=NON-stationarity (the opposite of ADF/PP)
non-rejection by ADF does not prove a unit root (low power) -> confirmatory KPSS
the p-value is clamped when the statistic falls outside the critical-value table
the payload is a flat record of atomic fields -> to_mcp recurses into them; there is no nested test object to unwrap
sources: Said & Dickey 1984 (Biometrika 71:599); Dickey & Fuller 1979 (JASA 74:427)
Kwiatkowski Phillips Schmidt Shin 1992 (J.Econometrics 54:159)
Phillips & Perron 1988 (Biometrika 75:335); Jarque & Bera 1987
Enders 2015 Applied Econometric Time Series 4th ed. ch.4

cards.method: Unit-root suite (ADF/KPSS/PP/ERS-DFGLS/Zivot-Andrews)
cards.when: heavy unit-root work with an explicit choice of deterministic model, DF-GLS (greater power), or Zivot-Andrews (ONE endogenous break)
cards.when_not: a fast yes/no with a p-value (-> #1); seasonal (-> #89); MULTIPLE breaks (-> #3); panel (-> #6)

alternatives.criterion: a fast ready-made p-value without the test regression
power is critical, series close to unity
ONE break at an unknown date (bpoint = the estimate)
multiple breaks

output_key_fields: teststat: numeric; cval: matrix of critical values 1/5/10% (-> nested rows+dim+axis labels)
model/type/lag: deterministic spec & lags (documents the decision)
bpoint (unitroot_zivot_andrews): estimated break position; tstats: rolling t-stat profile; yd (unitroot_dfgls): GLS-detrended
testreg/model/res: heavy lm/text -> stubbed by to_mcp
interpretation_traps: NO p-value: compare teststat with cval by hand
tail polarity: ADF/PP/ERS/ZA reject when teststat < cval (left tail); KPSS when teststat > cval (right tail)
the result carries the test regression alongside the statistic, not just a verdict; unitroot_zivot_andrews handles ONE break ONLY
sources: Elliott Rothenberg Stock 1996 (Econometrica 64(4):813, DF-GLS; cval MacKinnon 1991)
Zivot & Andrews 1992 (JBES 10(3):251)
KPSS 1992; Phillips & Perron 1988; Enders 2015 ch.4

cards.method: Structural change (Bai-Perron multiple breaks / Chow-F / CUSUM)
cards.when: testing & estimating the structural stability of a relationship; CUSUM (dating-free), sup-F (one break), Bai-Perron (multiple breaks + dates)
cards.when_not: only a unit-root yes/no (-> #1/#2); ONE break inside the unit-root framework (-> #2 unitroot_zivot_andrews); probabilistic regimes (Markov regimes, category 10; #30 covers gaussian/linear only); seasonality

alternatives.criterion: the break is tied to a unit-root question (one, endogenous)
smooth/probabilistic regime changes; #30 covers gaussian/linear only
CUSUM=screening without dating; Bai-Perron=how many & where, with dates

output_key_fields: breakpoints_minBIC: break index(es); breakdates: dates; confint: matrix lower/breakpoint/upper; confint_dates
process (run_fluctuation_process): the empirical fluctuation process as a series or frame (chart-ready); type; par (bandwidth, meaningless for CUSUM)
run_structural_change_test: atomic statistic/p_value/method/data_name = the main decision
breakpoints_full: heavy breakpointsfull -> stubbed
interpretation_traps: the par of run_fluctuation_process is NOT a decision; the decision is the p-value of run_structural_change_test
run_structural_change_test takes RAW Fstats/efp objects (not wrapper lists) — gate inherits
min-BIC may select 0 breaks (breakpoints_min_bic empty): no structural change, not an error
sources: Bai & Perron 1998 (Econometrica 66:47) & 2003 (J.Applied Econometrics 18:1)
Chow 1960 (Econometrica 28:591); Brown Durbin Evans 1975 (JRSS-B 37:149, CUSUM)
Andrews 1993 (Econometrica 61:821, sup-F)

cards.method: Seasonal adjustment with X-13ARIMA-SEATS
cards.when: seasonally adjusting a monthly/quarterly series + isolating trend/seasonal/irregular via regARIMA+SEATS/X-11
cards.when_not: TESTING a seasonal unit root (not adjustment -> #89); non-seasonal; no X-13 binaries (STL/10); structural breaks (-> #3)

alternatives.criterion: TESTING seasonal non-stationarity/stability (inference, not adjustment)
non-model-based decomposition, more robust than SEATS
trend extraction only (HP/Hamilton) without a seasonal model

output_key_fields: final: seasonally adjusted series (the main output, ts); original/trend/seasonal/irregular: components
seas_table: 'seats.seasonal'(s10) or 'x11.seasonal'(d10); None if no known spec
qs: QS seasonality test (post-check, small p = seasonality remains); udg: diagnostics
err/model/fivebestmdl: X-13 warnings, selected ARIMA, top-5
interpretation_traps: there is no seasonal extractor — the spec is auto-detected; seasonal is None when no SEATS spec was selected
final = original/(seasonal*trading-days); use get_x13_series(obj,'seats.adjustfac') for the ratio
final (adjusted) != trend (it has also removed the irregular)
sources: U.S. Census Bureau X-13ARIMA-SEATS Reference Manual
QS test: Maravall/Census diagnostics
precondition_tools: check_x13 (X-13 binaries installed/working before seas)

cards.method: Automatic outlier detection (Chen-Liu)
cards.when: automatic detection & classification of outliers (AO/LS/TC/IO/SLS) in a univariate ts before modelling; a level shift mimics a unit root
cards.when_not: a break in a regression relationship (-> #3); ONE unit-root break (-> #2 unitroot_zivot_andrews); outliers inside seasonal adjustment (-> #4); input that is not a time series

alternatives.criterion: structural change in a relationship, not isolated anomalies
outlier detection as part of seasonal adjustment
known ARIMA order, speed/stability

output_key_fields: outliers (data_frame): type/ind/time/coefhat/tstat (-> records) = the main result
yadj: series cleaned of outliers (ts); fit: final ARIMA; effects: contribution of the outliers
tsoutliers_object: the whole object (the docs do not enumerate named elements)
interpretation_traps: LS (level shift) != AO: a permanent level shift -> a possible structural break/pseudo unit root
before concluding I(1), check whether a single LS explains the non-stationarity
cval defaults from n (n<=50->3.0, n>=450->4.0); a larger n = a stricter threshold
exog_handle: EXPLICIT requirement of a matrix + column labels + the same start and frequency as y (gate stop)

cards.method: Panel unit-root (LLC/IPS/Fisher/Hadri + Pesaran CIPS)
cards.when: stationarity in a macro panel (i×t, large T); LLC/IPS/Fisher/Hadri (purtest) or CIPS (2nd generation, robust to cross-section dependence)
cards.when_not: univariate (-> #1/#2); ESTIMATING a panel equation FE/RE/GMM (-> category 08); panel cointegration; short-T micro panel

alternatives.criterion: CIPS under cross-sectional dependence; LLC/IPS when the units are independent
IPS heterogeneous root per unit; LLC a common root (more powerful if it holds)
confirmatory (H0 stationarity), as KPSS is against ADF

output_key_fields: run_panel_unit_root: a flat record {statistic, p_value, parameter, method, data_name, alternative}
args/idres: arguments + per-individual ADF regressions (records); adjval/sigma2 only for levinlin/ips
ips_tbar_crit: critical values only for ips_stat=tbar (lags=0)
run_cipstest: the whole test record
interpretation_traps: polarity: LLC/IPS/Fisher/CIPS have H0=unit root; BUT hadri has H0=stationarity (the opposite, like KPSS)
IPS non-rejection != all units I(1); it rejects if SOME units are stationary (heterogeneous alternative)
gate: ips_stat='tbar' does not apply when lags>0 (stop); tbar/hadri/levinlin not available for unbalanced panels
1st-generation purtest is size-distorted under cross-section dependence -> CIPS
sources: Levin Lin Chu 2002 (J.Econometrics 108:1); Im Pesaran Shin 2003 (115:53)
Maddala & Wu 1999 (Oxford Bull.Econ.Stat. 61:631); Choi 2001 (JIMF 20:249)
Hadri 2000 (Econometrics J. 3:148); Pesaran 2007 (J.Applied Econometrics 22:265, CIPS)
precondition_tools: make_panel_frame (panel structure before cipstest: pseries gate)
run_cipstest (model=cmg if cross-sectional dependence is present)

cards.method: Seasonal unit roots & seasonal stability (HEGY / Canova-Hansen)
cards.when: seasonal series (freq>1): stochastic/non-stationary seasonality (HEGY, H0 seasonal unit root) vs stable seasonality (Canova-Hansen, H0 stability)
cards.when_not: non-seasonal or level unit root only (-> #1/#2); REMOVING seasonality/adjustment (-> #4); panel (-> #6)

alternatives.criterion: opposite H0, as ADF+KPSS in the non-seasonal case
the final objective is the adjusted series
rough; HEGY however identifies AT WHICH frequency the root sits

output_key_fields: statistics: named numeric per root/frequency (t_1,t_2,F_3:4); pvalues; statistic_names
pvalue_method: RS (default) / raw / bootstrap (deterministic through the seed)
lag_method/lag_order/strdet/deterministic: the regression specification
test_object/fitted_model: stubbed by to_mcp
interpretation_traps: polarity: HEGY H0=unit root (small p=NO root); Canova-Hansen H0=stability (small p=changing) — OPPOSITE
HEGY = MANY verdicts (one per frequency); not one; a root may sit at a seasonal harmonic but not at zero frequency
deterministic=(0,0,0) is forbidden (it breaks the routine); bootstrap combined with AICc is forbidden
run_hegy_test computes its bootstrap p-value on the CPU; bootstrap=True selects it
sources: Hylleberg Engle Granger Yoo 1990 (J.Econometrics 44(1):215, HEGY)
Beaulieu & Miron 1993 (J.Econometrics 55:305); Smith Taylor del Barrio Castro 2009 (Econometric Theory 25:527)
Canova & Hansen 1995 (JBES 13(3):237); Burridge & Taylor 2004 (J.Econometrics 123:67, bootstrap)
Diaz-Emparanza 2014 (CSDA 76:237, response-surface p-values)

cards.method: Bootstrap unit-root tests robust to heterogeneity/non-stationary volatility/missing data (boot ADF / union / panel GM / order of integration)
cards.when: unit root/stationarity when the asymptotic critical values do not apply (heteroskedasticity/nonstationary volatility); a residual bootstrap instead of fixed tables; single series (boot_adf/boot_union), panel GM (boot_panel, H0=all have a UR), or the order of integration + stationarisation (order_integration -> diff_data feeder)
cards.when_not: fixed critical-value tables suffice -> #2/#1; KPSS, whose H0 is stationarity; seasonal roots -> #89 HEGY; a fixed-N panel -> #6; charts (the frontend); the raw joint and FDR routines as direct nodes (they are reachable only through boot_order_integration)

alternatives.criterion: robust to the arbitrary choice of deterministics/detrending (a union of 4 specs)
an a-priori specification; QD ⇒ DF-GLS, more powerful near unity
general and robust; the moving- and stationary-block bootstraps do NOT handle unbalanced data or gaps; the stationary and wild variants are not for panels
the asymptotic critical values do apply — faster, no bootstrap

output_key_fields: statistic/p_value/estimate (gamma; blank for the union test)/stationary/decision/selected_lag(s)/alpha/seed
boot_panel: statistic(Group-Mean)/some_stationary + individual_statistics/pvalues/estimates/selected_lags (N×specs matrices) + series_names
order_integration: order_int (named I(d) per series) + classification + diff_data (the stationarised TxN matrix — a PRODUCER, register->Parquet)
interpretation_traps: POLARITY: H0=unit root ⇒ p<alpha ⇒ STATIONARY (the OPPOSITE of KPSS, where rejection ⇒ non-stationary)
the panel H0 is that ALL series have a UR; rejection ⇒ SOME are stationary (NOT all) — run a per-series follow-up
the union test has no single gamma across the four combinations, so its estimate is blank by definition — NOT an error
gaps: a silent trim of the leading and trailing values, then an internal error -> a hard no-gaps gate (run #80 first)
the seed is MANDATORY (the bootstrap is stochastic); do_parallel=False for determinism and caching
sources: Smeekes & Wilms 2023 JSS 106(12):1-39 (bootstrap unit root tests)
Palm, Smeekes & Urbain 2011, J. Econometrics 163(1):85-104 (panel GM test)
Ng & Perron 2001, Econometrica 69(6):1519-1554 (MAIC lag selection)
Smeekes & Wijler 2020, Unit roots and cointegration (order of integration)
precondition_tools: boot_adf
boot_union

cards.method: Covariate-Augmented Dickey-Fuller (CADF) unit-root test — the power gain from stationary covariates (Hansen 1995); a plain ADF when no covariates are supplied
cards.when: a unit root in a univariate series when stationary, correlated covariates are available (CADF is more powerful than ADF); or a plain ADF with full p-values and automatic lag selection when no covariates are supplied
cards.when_not: no genuinely stationary covariate -> a plain ADF/PP (#1) or #2; H0 = stationarity, the reverse polarity -> KPSS; a seasonal unit root -> #89; a structural break -> unitroot_zivot_andrews; a non-stationary X invalidates the theory

alternatives.criterion: you want the classic critical-value tables without covariates
fast univariate screening without covariates
automatic lag selection within [min,max]; the default 'none' pins a fixed max_lag_y

output_key_fields: method (ADF|CADF)
statistic (+statistic_label)
p_value (Costantini-Lupi-Popp)
rho2 (the nuisance parameter, CADF only; absent for a plain ADF)
estimate
null_value
alternative=less
max_lag_y/min_lag_X/max_lag_X (as selected)
info_criteria {AIC,BIC,HQC,MAIC}
decision
warnings
interpretation_traps: POLARITY: H0=unit root, rejection (p<alpha) => STATIONARITY (the OPPOSITE of KPSS)
silently wrong (gated): a silent gap-drop in y; silent acceptance of gaps or a misaligned X; a cryptic out-of-bounds error on a constant y, on min_lag_X>max_lag_X, or on excessive lags
the «Specified sample size may be too small» notice is printed to stdout (it is NOT a raised warning) -> it is exposed in warnings; the p-value is less reliable at small n
min_lag_X<0 means leads of the covariates (a documented feature, not an error)
the covariates X MUST be stationary; a non-stationary X invalidates the asymptotic theory, and the routine does not check it
sources: Hansen BE (1995) Rethinking the Univariate Approach to Unit Root Testing, Econometric Theory 11(5):1148-1171
Costantini, Lupi, Popp (2007) A Panel-CADF Test for Unit Roots (asymptotic p-values)
Lupi 2009 JSS 32(2) (unit root CADF testing)
precondition_tools: c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test

cards.method: General-to-Specific (GETS) model selection + Indicator Saturation (IIS/SIS/TIS) for outliers & structural breaks
cards.when: set up the GUM (gts_ar_x: intercept+AR lags+regressors) -> a parsimonious final model (gts_model_selection, multi-path GETS+PET) or automatic detection of outliers/mean shifts/trend shifts (gts_indicator_saturation, IIS/SIS/TIS); deterministic (no seed)
cards.when_not: testing for a break at a single point with sup-F or CUSUM -> #3; ARIMA-intervention outliers -> #5; the log-variance variant is omitted; charts (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: a hypothesis-driven break test at a known or unknown point rather than automatic multiple saturation
an unknown number or location of breaks -> data-driven saturation with a controlled gauge (~t_pval·n false positives)

output_key_fields: coefficients + mean_results (term/coef/std_error/t_stat/p_value) + sigma/rss/logl/r_squared + fitted/residuals + n/k/df
gts_ar_x / gts_indicator_saturation: model = the fitted object (a producer, registered to the binary bucket; a stub once serialised)
gts_indicator_saturation: is_names (e.g. sis41), n_indicators, and the saturation dates per indicator type (breaks/date/index/coef/coef_se/coef_t/coef_p)
gts_model_selection: specific_spec (the regressor numbers kept), terminals_results, n_estimations, the empty_model flag
interpretation_traps: sisNN=a step shift at observation NN (a permanent level change); iisNN=an impulse (a single outlier); tisNN=a trend shift — do not confuse them
gauge: a tighter t_pval ⇒ fewer false detections and lower power; the saturation default is t_pval=0.001, NOT 0.05
gts_model_selection may end at the empty model -> empty_model=True with coefficients of length 0 (NOT a silent blank)
SILENTLY WRONG (gated): a regressor matrix with more rows than y is accepted silently; t_pval>=1 is accepted silently -> hard gates
sources: Pretis, Reade & Sucarrat (2018), JSS 86(3), doi:10.18637/jss.v086.i03
Sucarrat (2020), 12(2):388-401; Hendry & Doornik (2014), Empirical Model Discovery and Theory Evaluation (MIT Press)
precondition_tools: c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (stationarity of y before the GUM)

cards.method: Seasonality tests (combined/QS/Friedman/Kruskal-Wallis/seasonal-dummies/Welch/OCSB)
cards.when: the prechecks stage after stationarity (#1/#2), before seasonal adjustment (#3); the structural decision whether a monthly/quarterly/weekly series is seasonal; run_seasonality_test=a boolean gate (WO); ocsb=a seasonal unit root (nsdiffs)
cards.when_not: non-seasonal stationarity -> #1/#2; deseasonalisation -> X-13 (#4; this card only DETECTS); frequency=1 (a hard gate); charts (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: the objective is deseasonalization rather than detection
a suspected seasonal UNIT ROOT (stochastic) rather than deterministic seasonality
a fast default boolean decision (the WO combination rule)

output_key_fields: test/null_hypothesis/statistic/p_value/alpha/is_seasonal/decision/freq/n_obs (+ echoed args)
run_seasonality_test (combined): no single statistic; p_values carries the three named Webel-Ollech component p-values (QS, QS on the residuals, Kruskal-Wallis on the residuals)
ocsb: + method/augmentations/nrun/seed; the null is a seasonal unit root
interpretation_traps: POLARITY: combined/qs/fried/kw/seasdum/welch have H0=no seasonality (a small p => seasonal); ocsb has H0=A SEASONAL UNIT ROOT, REVERSED (fail to reject, p>=alpha => seasonal, the nsdiffs convention) -> which is why null_hypothesis is always returned
the combined test returns a LOGICAL decision (QS p<0.01 OR Kruskal-Wallis p<0.002), NOT a statistic; alpha does not affect it
gaps: SILENTLY WRONG — the tests accept them and return an incorrect decision -> a hard gate
isSeasonal does NOT support test='ocsb' (object 'seasonal' not found); run_seasonality_test routes ocsb directly
a pure deterministic sine is NOT detected by combined (it is residual-based); welch fails on a plain numeric ('intra' not found) -> normalise to a series
sources: Webel & Ollech (2019), An overall seasonality test, Deutsche Bundesbank Discussion Paper
Osborn, Chui, Smith & Birchenhall (1988), Seasonality and the order of integration for consumption, Oxford Bull. Econ. Stat. 50(4):361-377 (OCSB)

cards.method: Time-series decomposition (STL / classical) + feature extraction (STL strength / ACF / spectral entropy)
cards.when: a preparatory check of the structure of a seasonal series — isolating trend/seasonal/remainder (STL preferred, robust; classical as a baseline) or summarising into numeric features (trend/seasonal strength, ACF, spectral entropy) for screening/comparing series; a plain series input is converted to a keyed temporal table internally
cards.when_not: a non-seasonal series (frequency==1) -> the HP/BK/CF trend filters of category 10 (gated); forecasting with ARIMA/ETS -> category 02 (#7/#8); charts (the frontend); Box-Cox or Guerrero -> the transform nodes; multiple seasonal periods (a univariate series carries one frequency)

alternatives.criterion: STL is robust and loess-based (the default; s_window periodic or an odd number >=7); the classical decomposition is only a baseline (fixed seasonality, blanks at the edges)
you need the official X-13-ARIMA-SEATS seasonal adjustment rather than loess/MA
a non-seasonal trend/cycle rather than a seasonal decomposition
you want the raw ACF/PACF rather than unified comparable feature metrics

output_key_fields: components: data_frame {index, observed, trend, seasonal, remainder, season_adjust} (canonical, parquet-able)
strength (tsf_stl): {trend, seasonal} in [0,1]
decomp (tsf_stl/tsf_classical_decomposition): mable mdl_df [PRODUCER -> RDS bucket]
features (tsf_features): a named numeric list (one row) + feature_names + n_features
interpretation_traps: STL on frequency==1 SILENTLY drops the seasonal component -> a frequency>1 gate (do not read it as 'no seasonality')
STL or the classical decomposition on a series with gaps yields an empty model and then a cryptic component error -> a gap gate plus an empty-model post-gate
classical multiplicative on non-positive values -> a silently inconsistent decomposition -> a >0 gate
the column naming differs (STL season_year/remainder vs classical seasonal/random) -> unified to seasonal/remainder
the classical trend is blank over roughly frequency/2 observations at each edge, because of the centred moving average (expected, not an error)
a trend/seasonal strength ~1 => a strong component, ~0 => negligible
sources: Cleveland, Cleveland, McRae & Terpenning 1990, STL: A Seasonal-Trend Decomposition Procedure Based on Loess, J. Official Statistics 6:3-73
Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice 3e, ch.3 (decomposition & feature strengths), https://otexts.com/fpp3
precondition_tools: tsf_stl
tsf_classical_decomposition

cards.method: Data-driven locally-weighted regression decomposition of seasonality/trend (IPI optimal bandwidth) under short memory
cards.when: an equidistant seasonal ts (frequency>1); a non-parametric decomposition into trend + (slowly varying) seasonality + remainder with a DETERMINISTICALLY selected bandwidth (IPI/AMISE); it also returns detrended + seasonally-adjusted series
cards.when_not: frequency<=1 (non-seasonal -> a trend filter); the official model-based seasonal adjustment -> X-13 (#4); STL with explicit windows or robustness -> #126; charts (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: you want STL (loess) with explicit trend/seasonal windows or robustness to outliers rather than a data-driven optimal bandwidth
you need the official model-based X-13ARIMA-SEATS adjustment (RegARIMA+SEATS) rather than non-parametric locally-weighted regression

output_key_fields: trend/seasonal/remainder/observations: the series taken from the fitted decomposition (Trend/Seasonality/Rest/Observations)
detrended = observations - trend; adjusted = seasonally adjusted = observations - seasonality
bwidth: the relative [0,1] data-driven IPI bandwidth (NOT a number of observations); sum_autocov: the estimated sum of autocovariances
model: the fitted decomposition object (a producer -> a binary pointer)
interpretation_traps: the routine accepts a matrix SILENTLY (silently wrong) — the wrapper blocks multivariate input
bwidth is a RELATIVE bandwidth, not a number of observations
a gap gives the cryptic «Convergence of the bandwidth selection algorithm failed» (gated); the seasonality is assumed to vary SLOWLY
sources: Feng, Gries & Fritz (2020), Data-driven local polynomial for the trend and its derivatives, J. Nonparametric Statistics 32(2):510-533
Feng (2013), J. Applied Statistics 40(2):266-281; Bühlmann (1996), J. Time Series Analysis 17(3):247-270
precondition_tools: c01_preparation_prechecks/seasonality.run_seasonality_test (seasonality is present)

cards.method: Detection of structural breaks in the trend & seasonality of seasonal time series (BFAST: iterative STL + breakpoints) + near-real-time disturbance monitoring
cards.when: a seasonal ts (frequency>1); locating WHEN the trend and/or the seasonality changed structurally (retrospective multiple breaks + dates, bfast_detect) or near-real-time detection of a new disturbance at the end (bfast_monitor); separating trend/season before forecasting/regime work
cards.when_not: a non-seasonal series (frequency=1); only a unit-root yes/no -> #1/#2; one break inside the unit-root framework -> unitroot_zivot_andrews (#2); probabilistic regimes (Markov switching); charts (the frontend); gaps without an explicit gap-tolerant decomposition (a gated silent fallback)

alternatives.criterion: Bai-Perron dating of ONE relationship/trend (a regression) only, without a seasonal decomposition & seasonal breaks
a smooth (data-driven bandwidth) trend+seasonal decomposition WITHOUT break detection
online detection of a new disturbance at the END, not a full retrospective break history

output_key_fields: trend_breaks/seasonal_breaks: {n, indices, dates (decimal time), confint(lower/break/upper_date)}
magnitude/time_of_change: the largest change & its timing, for the TREND ONLY (Vt)
trend_component/seasonal_component/remainder_component: ts chart-data (the last iteration)
model: the full fit (a producer -> the 'model' register field, a binary bucket; a stub once serialised)
bfast_monitor: breakpoint (a date, or blank), disturbance (a boolean), magnitude = median(data - prediction), history_period/monitor_period
interpretation_traps: the breakpoints are positions within the gap-free component series, NOT raw positions — the node already returns them as dates
no break: the no-breakpoint flags are set, so the breakpoint fields come back blank rather than as a breakpoint object -> n=0 and empty fields
magnitude/time_of_change concern the TREND ONLY, not the seasonality
gaps with decomp='stl' fall back silently to the gap-tolerant decomposition (gated: ask for it explicitly)
sources: Verbesselt et al. (2010) Detecting trend and seasonal changes, Remote Sensing of Environment 114(1):106-115
Verbesselt et al. (2010) Phenological change detection, RSE 114(12):2970-2980
Verbesselt, Zeileis, Herold (2012) Near real-time disturbance detection, RSE 123:98-108
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/series_layout_conversion.ts_fill_regular (a regular series before the break detection)
c00_data_utilities/series_layout_conversion.ts_convert (to a series with frequency>1)
c00_data_utilities/replacement_missing_values.impute_kalman (fill the gaps; otherwise use the gap-tolerant decomposition)

cards.method: Regularisation/decomposition & analysis of space-time series (turning points + Kendall info; a full descriptive table including normality; diff/LOESS trend-seasonal decomposition)
cards.when: a preparatory diagnostic BEFORE estimation: a full descriptive table (ps_descriptives) with normality criteria; locating peaks and pits plus a randomness test (ps_turning_points, the Kendall information); fast detrending or a seasonal loess decomposition (ps_decompose)
cards.when_not: charts (the frontend); formal stationarity or unit-root testing -> #1/#2; the seasonal HEGY/CH tests -> #89; multiplicative seasonal adjustment -> #4; irregular-to-regular resampling WAS OMITTED

alternatives.criterion: you want ACF/PACF/rolling/correlation rather than a static summary table per series
you need a formal stationarity p-value rather than a turning-point/visual precheck
you want a full X-13 seasonal adjustment rather than a quick decdiff/decloess

output_key_fields: ps_turning_points: n_turns/n_peaks/n_pits/first_is_peak; tppos + peak_positions/pit_positions; proba/info (if calc_proba) — info=-log2(P), larger ⇒ more monotone/informative

cards.method: MULTIVARIATE outlier detection: CLASSICAL Mahalanobis distances vs the ROBUST MCD (Deterministic MCD) at the SAME chi-square(p) cutoff + a MASKING / SWAMPING diagnostic
cards.when: a numeric observations×variables matrix (countries × macro indicators, periods × variables) and the question is WHICH ROWS are outlying in the JOINT (multivariate) space — a COMBINATION of values that no univariate check sees (each individual value «normal», the combination impossible); the flow: mv_outliers (classical AND robust SIDE BY SIDE + masked/swamped) -> mv_mcd (only the robust center/cov/h/best subset) -> mv_mahalanobis (the classical distance, or OUT-OF-SAMPLE scoring with a GIVEN center/cov)
cards.when_not: ONE variable (p >= 2 is a hard gate; univariate tails or capping -> #114); TIME-SERIES outliers of type AO/LS/TC/IO in a univariate series -> #5; the LEVELS of non-stationary series, where a Mahalanobis distance is UNINTERPRETABLE — the population mean does not exist and the sample covariance diverges with T, so supply differences EXPLICITLY (§3b gate 3); missing data (impute FIRST, category 00); CLUSTERING rather than outlier detection -> category 29 (#241, #244); charts (the frontend, §5); robust REGRESSION — a different family (categories 06/07)

alternatives.alt: mv_outliers (the MAIN function of the card)
alternatives.criterion: you want THE DECISION: the classical AND robust distances at the same cutoff + masked/swamped counts + a ranking by decreasing robust D². It is the default path — the comparison of the two IS the result
you want ONLY the ROBUST center/cov (e.g. as fitted parameters for downstream scoring) with MAXIMUM robustness: h ~ n/2, a breakdown point of ~ (n-h+1)/n
you know the contamination is < 25% and you want HIGHER EFFICIENCY (a larger h) with less robustness — alpha controls EXACTLY that trade-off
the sample is PROVABLY clean (or you want the baseline for the comparison): purely algebraic, with no randomness and no MCD
an OUT-OF-SAMPLE APPLY (§3b gate 6): you pass back the center/cov of a previous mv_mcd => robust scoring of NEW observations; with BOTH supplied, n >= 1 suffices
the objective is UNIVARIATE tail cleaning per series (capping/trimming), not the detection of outlying COMBINATIONS
the input is a TIME SERIES and outliers are wanted BY TYPE (additive / level shift / transitory change), not by a multivariate distance

output_key_fields: mv_mahalanobis: distance (the named D² per observation — the main chart-data) + distance_sqrt + outlier/outlier_index/outlier_labels + n_outliers/share_outliers + cutoff = qchisq(quantile, df = p) + df = p + center/cov/cov_rcond + center_source/cov_source ('sample' or 'supplied') + max_distance/n/p/observations/variables

mv_mcd: center and cov (ROBUST, fit and apply) + cov_rcond + cor, ONLY when robust_cor=True and absent otherwise, + distance and raw_distance, after and before the reweighting, + raw_center and raw_cov + outlier/n_outliers/share_outliers + h, the subset size implied by alpha, n and p, with h_share, best_subset and in_best_subset + mcd_weight, binary 0/1, with n_zero_weight + crit, the log determinant, + cnp2 and raw_cnp2, the consistency and finite-sample factors, of length 2, + method, a deterministic subsampling scheme, i_best (1 to 6) and n_csteps per initial subset + small_sample (n < 2p) + alpha, use_correction and seed

mv_outliers: distance_table (an n×2 «classical | robust» table — THE CENTRAL chart-data) + classical/robust + outlier_classical/outlier_robust + masked / swamped / both (+ n_ and _labels for each) + order_robust / ranked_labels (by decreasing robust D², ties broken on the name) + classical_center/classical_cov/classical_rcond + robust_center/robust_cov/robust_rcond + h/h_share/best_subset/in_best_subset/mcd_weight/crit + cutoff/quantile/df/alpha/use_correction/small_sample/seed
ALL of them: observations/variables (the row/column names; if they are missing, obs1.obsN / v1.vP are generated) — every flag/distance is named PER ROW
interpretation_traps: MASKING AND SWAMPING ARE THE POINT OF THIS NODE: the classical mean and covariance are computed FROM the outlying points themselves, so an outlier «hides» itself by inflating the variance, while clean points look outlying. The MCD estimates from the «cleanest» subset h, so it is not corrupted. Do NOT read ONLY the classical column: read n_masked and n_swamped (live in the tests, the classical method found 2 of the 4 planted outliers while the MCD found all 4 — and no univariate check would have seen any of them)

alpha STRICTLY in [0.5, 1) — SILENTLY WRONG: the MCD routine(alpha = 0.2) does NOT error, it only warns «subsample size h < n/2 may be too small» and returns a fit with h = 9 out of 30 (a breakdown point > 50%: the «robust» subset can be ENTIRELY outlying). The reference documentation states «Allowed values are between 0.5 and 1» => OUR OWN hard gate

alpha = 1 DEGENERACY (a separate hard gate): «alpha = 1: The minimum covariance determinant estimates... are equal to the classical estimates», and the result then carries NO distance, best-subset or best-index fields AT ALL (live-verified) — zero robustness AND no distance

DETERMINISM (§5): the deterministic subsampling scheme is PINNED — the Deterministic MCD, which starts from the h most central points of SIX deterministic estimators; the alternative default draws 500 random subsamples. The seed is a SAFETY NET above the subsample threshold (1500 with the defaults), where the documentation states explicitly that «the initial search uses only a subsample»; it runs with the generator seeded and the caller's state RESTORED afterwards, keeping the layer pure. Live: identical over two runs, AND identical distances under a DIFFERENT seed

mcd_weight against outlier: the weights are binary and tied to the FIXED 0.975 cutoff of the original weight function — INDEPENDENT of our own 'quantile'. With a quantile other than 0.975, n_zero_weight does NOT equal n_outliers; that is not an error, it is a different cutoff

SILENTLY WRONG cases blocked by hard gates: p = 1, where the estimator does NOT error but returns a result WITHOUT any distance or best subset — a univariate path; a text column in a frame, which is silently coerced and then worked on as category CODES (live, a criterion of -2.300799); gaps, NaN and infinities, which SILENTLY drop rows; n <= p, or n == p+1, which give the cryptic «n <= p -- you can't be serious!» and «n == p+1 is too small sample size for MCD»; and a constant column or collinearity, where the distance fails with «system is exactly singular» or «system is computationally singular» — pre-checked against machine epsilon and exposed as cov_rcond

NO STANDARDIZATION, NO transform ARGUMENT (§3b gate 2): the Mahalanobis distance is AFFINE EQUIVARIANT — D²(x) = D²(Ax+b) — so scale(X) gives IDENTICAL distances (classical AND MCD, live-verified). A transform argument would be a no-op that implied a choice which does not exist

NON-STATIONARITY (§3b gate 3, Hamilton-Ma-Xi): this node is CROSS-SECTION / PANEL. On the LEVELS of I(1) series the population mean is undefined and the sample covariance diverges with T => the distances are uninterpretable. The user supplies differences EXPLICITLY — NEVER a silent correction here

cnp2 and raw_cnp2 have LENGTH 2 — the consistency factor AND the finite-sample correction (Pison et al. 2002); with use_correction=False the second element becomes 1. small_sample=True (n < 2p) corresponds to the «n < 2 * p» warning — a DIAGNOSTIC, not a gate

raw_distance against distance: distance is AFTER the reweighting, and typically considerably more efficient (Pison et al. 2002), while raw_distance is before it. best_subset and h ALWAYS refer to the RAW step, and the subset length equals the h implied by alpha, n and p — post-checked

a TERMINAL node (no register/handle chaining): it returns chart-ready numbers. The fit/apply split is EXPLICIT — the user passes center/cov back into mv_mahalanobis (modelled on the KNIME «Normalize Model»)
sources: the MCD routine (live, in the engine) — «Allowed values are between 0.5 and 1 and the default is 0.5»; the deterministic scheme «starts from the h most central observations of six (deterministic) estimators»; «When nmini*kmini < n, the initial search uses only a subsample of size nmini*kmini»; the retained count equals the h implied by alpha, n and p, and the best subset has exactly that length; the best index runs from 1 to 6, with a concentration-step count per initial subset; cnp2 holds the consistency and finite-sample factors; and the weight function is the original 0/1 rule (Rousseeuw & Van Driessen 1999)
Rousseeuw, P.J. & Van Driessen, K. (1999) «A fast algorithm for the minimum covariance determinant estimator», Technometrics 41, 212-223 (FastMCD)

Hubert, M., Rousseeuw, P.J. & Verdonck, T. (2012) «A deterministic algorithm for robust location and scatter», Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 21, 618-637 (DetMCD = the PINNED nsamp)
Pison, Van Aelst & Willems 2002, Metrika 55:111-123 (small sample corrections for LTS and MCD) — use_correction, cnp2, and the efficiency of the reweighting
Rousseeuw, P.J. & Leroy, A.M. (1987) Robust Regression and Outlier Detection, Wiley (the breakdown point; why the classical mean/cov collapses in the presence of outliers)

Hamilton, J.D., Ma, X. & Xi, J., «Principal Component Analysis for a Mix of Stationary and Nonstationary Variables», NBER WP 32068 — §3b gate 3 (why this node is cross-section/panel and not for the levels of I(1) series)

the normative gate spec §3b live-verified gates («the MCD routine: n == p+1 is too small sample size for MCD; alpha in [0.5,1]»; «the MCD routine(alpha=0.2) -> only a warning»; «mahalanobis with n<=p or collinear columns -> system is computationally singular»); DETERMINISM: «the MCD routine ⇒ nsamp="deterministic"»

cards.method: A battery of NORMALITY tests (the composite hypothesis): EDF omnibus tests (Anderson-Darling / Cramer-von Mises / Lilliefors) + the Pearson chi-square test on equiprobable classes + Shapiro-Francia, with a COMMON alpha and a long-format decision table
cards.when: ONE numeric univariate series (typically model RESIDUALS, returns, a macro series) and the question is whether its DISTRIBUTION is normal, with the parameters UNKNOWN (the composite hypothesis); nt_normality_battery = ALL the requested tests in ONE call -> a long-format table (statistic/p_value/decision) + a consensus summary; the 5 individual functions when you want ONE specific test (or when n rules some of them out)
cards.when_not: JARQUE-BERA, the moment-based test on skewness and kurtosis, ALREADY EXISTS as #1 run_jarque_bera_test and is NOT duplicated here (and BEWARE the incompatible missing-value policy — see the traps); a DESCRIPTIVE Shapiro-Wilk inside a descriptives table, with no gates and no decision -> #129 ps_descriptives; DESCRIPTIVE moments per column -> #248 dp_profile; SEVERAL columns at once (run the node PER COLUMN — a hard gate against a matrix or frame); missing values (impute FIRST, category 00 — a hard stop here); testing STATIONARITY (#1/#2) or AUTOCORRELATION (Ljung-Box; #81 desc_acf), which are different hypotheses; quantile plots (the frontend, §5); MULTIVARIATE normality -> #246

alternatives.criterion: you want THE DECISION with cross-checking: a long-format table + a consensus (reject_all / fail_to_reject_all / mixed) + a primary_test by a DOCUMENTED order of preference
ONE test, the RECOMMENDED EDF test after Stephens (1986); it gives MORE WEIGHT TO THE TAILS => the first choice when fat tails are the concern (returns, crises); it requires n > 7
a correlation-based test «known to perform well» (Royston 1993); the SECOND choice in the order of preference; it requires 5 <= n <= 5000 (it is RULED OUT for large samples)
an EDF omnibus test, the «second choice» after Anderson-Darling; it puts less weight on the tails and requires n > 7
the literature/reader asks for it explicitly (the best-known EDF test) — BUT it is «known to perform worse» than AD/CvM; it is the ONLY one that works for 5 <= n <= 7

alternatives.alt: nt_pearson_test, with adjust both True and False
alternatives.criterion: you want the chi-square test on equiprobable classes; it is «usually not recommended» (inferior power) AND the correct p-value is NEITHER of the two — it lies BETWEEN them (Moore 1986) => run it BOTH ways
you want a test of MOMENTS (skewness and kurtosis) rather than a deviation of the DISTRIBUTION FUNCTION — COMPLEMENTARY, not a substitute; CAUTION: a different missing-value policy

output_key_fields: nt_normality_battery: table = long-format records (test/test_label/method/statistic/statistic_name/p_value/df/n_classes/expected_per_class/n/alpha/reject/decision) — THE MAIN chart-data; the row order is CANONICAL (ad,cvm,lillie,pearson,sf) regardless of the order the user supplied

nt_normality_battery summary: statistic/p_value/reject, named PER TEST, + n_tests/n_reject/share_reject/reject_any/reject_all + consensus ('reject_all', 'fail_to_reject_all' or 'mixed') + min/max/median_p_value + primary_test/primary_p_value/primary_reject + alpha/n/mean/sd/series/na_policy='error' + results, the complete per-test output including the raw test record

the individual tests: test/test_label/method/statistic/statistic_name/p_value/alpha/reject/decision ('reject_normality' or 'fail_to_reject') + interpretation, a ready-made sentence, + n/series/na_policy + the raw test record
the Pearson chi-square ONLY: df / n_classes / expected_per_class / adjust / min_expected (blank in the other tests, which is how you see that they do NOT apply)
interpretation_traps: MIN-N PER TEST, NEVER A GLOBAL n (live-verified messages): Anderson-Darling and Cramér-von Mises need n > 7 («sample size must be greater than 7»); Lilliefors needs n > 4; Shapiro-Francia needs 5 <= n <= 5000 («sample size must be between 5 and 5000» — it RULES OUT large samples too); the Pearson chi-square has NO gate of its own (see below). In the battery there is NO silent skip: if a requested test does not fit, the call STOPS and the user removes it EXPLICITLY from 'tests' (blocked-by-gate, §5)

AN INCOMPATIBLE MISSING-VALUE POLICY — AN EXPLICIT PROJECT DECISION: the EDF tests declare «Missing values are allowed» and SILENTLY drop the incomplete cases (live, a gap in the input still returns a normal-looking result), whereas the EXISTING Jarque-Bera node (#1) ERRORS. On the SAME input the two normality nodes would give one result and one error, and the reported n would NOT be the n of the input, so the min-n gates would be read wrongly. THE CHOICE: ONE policy, the STRICTER one — a HARD STOP, with a message pointing at the imputation path (category 00); na_policy='error' is ALWAYS returned in the output

THE SILENTLY-WRONG CASES OF nt_pearson_test (the underlying routine has NO validity check at all): (a) n_classes = 3 with adjust=True gives df = 0 and therefore p = 0 EXACTLY, for ANY data (live, a p-value of 0 on NORMAL data); (b) n_classes = 2 with adjust=True gives df = -1, a «NaNs produced» warning and a blank p; (c) a non-integer n_classes such as 4.7 is accepted SILENTLY and truncated when the counts are formed; (d) an expected frequency n/k below 5 breaks the chi-square approximation (Cochran 1954; Moore 1986) and nothing warns; (e) an extreme value whose normal CDF is exactly 1 lands in a class beyond the last and is DROPPED from the counts (live, 199 counted for n = 200, WITH NO warning). EACH ONE is a hard gate here, with the PERMITTED RANGE of n_classes inside the message

the Pearson adjust switch: NEITHER of the two p-values is the correct one — «this is not (!) the correct p-value, lying somewhere between the two»; adjust=True gives df = k-3, correcting for the two estimated parameters, and False gives df = k-1. Run BOTH and read them as BOUNDS: the statistic is THE SAME, and only the degrees of freedom and the p-value change (live-verified)

Lilliefors != ks_test: «Although the test statistic obtained from lillie_test(x) is the same as that obtained from ks_test(x, "pnorm", mean(x), sd(x)), it is not correct to use the p-value from the latter for the composite hypothesis of normality (mean and variance unknown), since the distribution of the test statistic is different when the parameters are estimated» (the lillie_test routine). NEVER compare the two p-values

Shapiro-FRANCIA is NOT Shapiro-WILK: this card exposes Shapiro-Francia, the squared correlation with the expected normal quantiles; the Shapiro-Wilk test is NOT exposed as inference by any node — it appears ONLY descriptively in #129 ps_descriptives, with no gates and no decision

THE ORDER OF PREFERENCE (primary_test) IS DOCUMENTED, NOT ARBITRARY: ad > sf > cvm > lillie > pearson, taken from the documented Notes themselves («the recommended EDF test by Stephens (1986)»; «known to perform well.. Royston (1993)»; «as second choice»; «known to perform worse»; «usually not recommended.. inferior power properties»). primary_test is the FIRST available one of that order inside the selected subset

consensus = 'mixed' IS A NORMAL RESULT, not an error: the tests have DIFFERENT power against different departures (tails vs the centre vs moments). Live in the tests: with an alpha BETWEEN the p-values of ad (9.73e-05) and cvm (4.59e-04) ONLY ad rejects (n_reject = 1, share = 0.2). Read primary_test + the WHOLE table, never a single cell

fail_to_reject DOES NOT PROVE NORMALITY (the interpretation field itself says so explicitly); it is the absence of EVIDENCE against normality at the given n. alpha changes ONLY the decision column — NEVER the p_value

OTHER silently-wrong cases that are blocked: an infinity in the input makes Anderson-Darling, Cramér-von Mises and Lilliefors fail with a cryptic type error, while Shapiro-Francia returns NaN and the Pearson chi-square returns a NORMAL-LOOKING statistic of 21 with p = 0.00032, NEITHER of them raising an error or a warning; ZERO VARIANCE makes the first three fail cryptically, Shapiro-Francia warn and return a blank, and the Pearson chi-square produce a FALSELY «significant» result with nothing at all — the worst of the family; and a matrix or frame is a hard stop, since the node runs PER COLUMN

DETERMINISM (§5): no RNG in any of the 5 tests (closed-form formulas/tables from Stephens 1986, Dallal-Wilkinson 1986, Royston 1993, chi-square) => NO seed; identical over 2 runs AND identical output regardless of the order of 'tests'

Compared to the Anderson-Darling test and the Cramer-von Mises test it is known to perform worse»; and the explicit warning that the plain Kolmogorov-Smirnov p-value does not apply to the composite hypothesis

interpretation_traps: AN EXPLICIT DEFINITION OF THE MOMENTS (NEVER «just skewness»): Joanes & Gill (1998), the standard three-type typology. m_r = (1/n) * sum (x_i - xbar)^r, the MOMENT estimator with divisor n rather than n-1. type1 (THE DEFAULT): g1 = m3/m2^(3/2), g2 = m4/m2^2 - 3; type2 (SAS and SPSS): G1 = g1*sqrt(n(n-1))/(n-2) for n>=3, G2 = ((n+1)g2+6)(n-1)/((n-2)(n-3)) for n>=4; type3 (Minitab and BMDP): b1 = g1*((n-1)/n)^(3/2), b2 = (g2+3)(1-1/n)^2 - 3. THE KURTOSIS IS ALWAYS EXCESS — 0 under normality — in ALL THREE types, and that is declared explicitly as kurtosis_excess=True

COMPARABILITY: OUR default is type1, whereas other implementations default to type = 3 — TWO «skewness» values on the same data can differ because the ESTIMATOR changed, not the data. That is why moment_type/quantile_type/kurtosis_excess are ALWAYS returned (§3b gate 6). The tests pin identity against an INDEPENDENT recomputation AND against an independent implementation for all 3 types

NO SILENT COERCION (§3b gate 2): the non-numeric columns get the COUNT fields and a blank for the moments — they are NEVER turned into numbers. An UNKNOWN column dtype (a duration, a time-indexed value, a unit-carrying value, a labelled value) is a HARD STOP: it was LIVE-VERIFIED as silently wrong that a duration is stored as a double, so without the gate it would be profiled as «numeric» with moments in UNKNOWN UNITS, days or seconds. The same stop covers a nested-list column, a frame column, a matrix column, a decomposed timestamp, and a complex column

NEVER NaN OR INFINITY IN THE OUTPUT (the dp_postcheck_finite check): the DOCUMENTED silently-wrong behaviours that are neutralised — the minimum or maximum of an ALL-MISSING column returns plus or minus infinity, with the warning «no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf», and here comes back blank; the moments of a constant column divide zero by zero and give NaN, and here come back blank; and a NUMERIC OVERFLOW, say 1e308 against -1e308, gives an infinite standard deviation WITHOUT an error, which here BLOCKS, since the profile would be numerically meaningless

NaN COUNTS AS MISSING, an infinity does NOT — it is counted separately in n_infinite, excluded from the moments AND flagged as a blocker. n_valid counts the values that are both present and finite. n_unique counts the DISTINCT present values — for a categorical column the levels actually PRESENT, not the declared level count, which is exposed separately as n_levels in dp_column_profile

EDGE-CASE BEHAVIOUR (documented and tested): an ALL-MISSING column gives n_unique = 0, a blank is_constant rather than False, and blank moments; a single valid value makes the minimum, quartiles, median, mean and maximum coincide, the interquartile range 0, and the standard deviation and both shape moments blank; a constant column gives a standard deviation of 0 but blank skewness and kurtosis, since the second moment is 0; and n_zeros is blank for NON-numeric columns, where «zero» is undefined

THE MOMENTS ARE DESCRIPTIVE, NOT INFERENCE: on an AUTOCORRELATED series they are NOT evidence of normality, nor a basis for a test (§3b gate 4: autocorrelation inflates the Type I error). For a normality decision -> #247 or #1; for inference under autocorrelation -> the HAC path (#35, category 07)

THE HISTOGRAM IS NOT THE CONVENTIONAL ONE: the Sturges breaks there are prettified, giving an UNPREDICTABLE number of bins; here they are EXACTLY equal-width, spanning the minimum to the maximum in bins+1 edges, and therefore reproducible. A constant column, where the minimum equals the maximum, gives ONE degenerate bin (degenerate=True) rather than degenerate equal breaks. A post-check confirms that the counts sum to the number of values, so nothing is lost. NO DRAWING — only breaks, counts and midpoints (§5)

dp_quality_flags: THE RULES ARE EXPLICIT AND SOURCED — all_missing (a blocker); high_missing above max_missing_pct (a warning; the default is 10%, the Bennett 2001 rule the detail itself cites); constant (a blocker: a correlation returns a blank with ONLY a warning, and a z-score divides by 0); infinite_values (a blocker); high_cardinality at or above max_unique_ratio (a warning: it looks like an identifier, not a variable); duplicate_rows (a warning: it breaks k-means with «more cluster centers than distinct data points», and non-metric scaling with «zero or negative distance»); few_rows below min_rows (a warning: the min-n of the normality tests); p_ge_n (a blocker: a singular covariance makes the Mahalanobis distance report «system is computationally singular», and model-based clustering does not even error); and no_complete_rows (a blocker). all_missing EXCLUDES high_missing — one flag per column for missingness

cards.method: Analysis of MISSINGNESS PATTERNS (CROSS-VARIABLE): a pattern matrix, 1 observed and 0 missing, + the counts per pattern + an EXACT MONOTONICITY check (Van Buuren) · the gap runs and spans per variable (a ragged edge, or mixed frequency) · co-missingness per PAIR (rr/rm/mr/mm)
cards.when: the question is NOT «how many are missing PER COLUMN» — that is #248 — but «WHICH COMBINATIONS of variables are missing TOGETHER»: 10% missing across 5 variables may be ONE common pattern, the same 10 countries, or 5 DISJOINT ones, giving 40% incomplete rows. The flow: mp_pattern (how many DISTINCT patterns, how many complete cases, and MONOTONICITY) -> mp_runs (WHERE the gaps sit in time: leading, internal or trailing, so mixed frequency against a ragged edge from a publication lag) -> mp_pairs (which PAIRS are missing together). It works on MIXED column types — the criterion is ONLY whether a value is present, with no coercion
cards.when_not: IMPUTATION, dropping rows or columns, or any alteration — the node DIAGNOSES (§3b gate 2; filling gaps in a time series -> #80); a per-column profile with moments, types and quality flags -> #248 («one wrapper = one node»); ESTIMATION with a ragged edge or mixed frequency, rather than DIAGNOSIS -> #15/#17/#18/#144; an MCAR TEST (Little 1988) — NOT exposed, since it requires normality and EM, and the autocorrelation of macro panels violates the assumptions (§3b gate 4); charts (the frontend, §5 — the node supplies ONLY the 0/1 matrices, the counts and the spans); data with no column names, or with DUPLICATE ones, where the patterns would be ambiguous

alternatives.criterion: you want the STRUCTURE of the missingness: how many DISTINCT patterns exist, how many rows per pattern, how many complete cases, and whether the pattern is MONOTONE (critical for which imputation mechanism is admissible)

the data are TIME-ORDERED and you want to know WHERE the gaps are: a trailing gap is a ragged edge from a publication lag, a leading gap a series that starts later, and an internal gap either mixed frequency or a silent hole. The pattern matrix does NOT distinguish the three cases

you want the PER-PAIR view: rr means both observed; rm the row observed and the column missing; mr the reverse; mm both missing — which shows which pairs NEVER have observations in common, since rr = 0 means no pairwise correlation is defined

you want the conventional MEANING of the row ordering, «increasing amounts of missing information»; the default, 'count', orders by a DECREASING number of rows, the most frequent pattern first. BOTH are TOTAL orderings with a complete tie-break, which the conventional implementation does not define
a STRICTLY INCREASING time column exists: it is excluded from the variables (it is the axis) and the spans get start_time/end_time LABELS; without it the positions are plain row indices
you need counts+moments PER COLUMN (#248) or the FILLING of the gaps (#80) — #249 NEVER alters the data

monotone (mp_pattern): {is_monotone, order — the names in the MONOTONE ordering — order_index, n_violating_rows, pct_violating_rows, first_violating_row}; an EXACT check, not a heuristic

summary (mp_pattern): {n_rows, n_cols, n_patterns, n_complete_cases, n_incomplete_cases, pct_complete_cases, n_cells, n_missing_cells, pct_missing_cells, n_cols_with_missing, n_all_missing_cols, n_complete_cols, any_missing}

mp_runs: runs is a long-format record set, ONE PER GAP SPAN {variable, run_id, start, end, length, position — leading, internal, trailing or all — start_time, end_time} + variables (with n_runs, longest_run, leading_na, trailing_na, n_internal_runs, n_internal_missing, first_obs and last_obs with their times, is_all_missing, is_complete) + na_counts_by_row

mp_pairs: rr / rm / mr / mm (FOUR p x p INTEGER matrices with axis labels — chart-data) + pairs (long-format records i<j {variable_1, variable_2, both_observed, both_missing, only_1_missing, only_2_missing, pct_both_missing}) + summary {n_pairs, n_pairs_co_missing, max_both_missing}

ALL of them: columns (ALWAYS in the INPUT ORDER) + time_name (+ sort_by in mp_pattern, time_labels in mp_runs) — §3b gate 6: ALL the parameters that determine the output are returned, so that two runs are COMPARABLE
interpretation_traps: WHY THE STANDARD LIBRARY AND NOT A MISSING-DATA DEPENDENCY (the normative gate spec §3b REJECTED it — a DOCUMENTED DECISION): we take the SEMANTICS of the pattern and pair matrices WITHOUT the dependency, because (a) it would shadow common verbs in the SHARED source environment and (b) its pattern function DRAWS by default, violating charter §5, «charts ONLY in the frontend». Here: ZERO new dependencies, ZERO drawing, only numeric chart data. The ENCODING — 1 observed, 0 missing — and the rr/rm/mr/mm convention are preserved

A DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE FROM THE CONVENTIONAL IMPLEMENTATION: (i) the counts are NOT appended as the LAST ROW and COLUMN of the same matrix, since they would pollute the chart data with non-binary values — they are SEPARATE fields, pattern_counts and variables; (ii) the COLUMNS are NEVER reordered, whereas the conventional implementation «sorts rows and columns in increasing amounts of missing information», so the SAME schema with different data would give a DIFFERENT column order, and incomparable runs

A DETERMINISTIC ORDERING — AN EXPLICIT RULE (no RNG anywhere): the COLUMNS are ALWAYS in the input order. The pattern ROWS use THREE keys: sort_by='count' (default) => DECREASING count -> INCREASING n_missing_vars -> INCREASING pattern key; sort_by='missingness' => INCREASING n_missing_vars -> DECREASING count -> INCREASING pattern key. The pattern key is UNIQUE per pattern ⇒ the ordering is TOTAL (no tie is left unresolved). RUNS: the input order of the variables, then INCREASING start. PAIRS: DECREASING both_missing -> INCREASING i -> INCREASING j. ALL with method='radix' = the C locale ⇒ locale-independent (live-verified: order(c('a','B'), method='radix') = 2,1 whereas the default en_US gives 1,2)

MONOTONICITY — WHAT IT MEANS AND WHY THE CHECK IS EXACT: the Van Buuren definition (FIMD 2nd ed., §4.1.1) — «A missing data pattern is said to be monotone if the variables Y_j can be ordered such that if Y_j is missing then all variables Y_k with k>j are also missing». Equivalently: the sets M_j = {i : Y_ij is missing} are NESTED. The node does NOT search over p! orderings: it checks ONE (increasing |M_j|) and that SUFFICES, because nested sets have increasing cardinality and equinumerous nested sets are EQUAL. The tests verify this against a BRUTE-FORCE search over all p! orderings

THE DEFINITION OF MISSING (explicit, NEVER «just missingness»): a cell is missing when it holds no value. NaN COUNTS as missing (live-verified) while an infinity does NOT — an infinity is a VALUE. For infinity diagnostics -> #248 dp_profile, the n_infinite field

WHY THERE IS A GATE FOR A STRICTLY INCREASING TIME COLUMN: the gap runs and spans are defined ONLY when the row order IS the time order. With an unsorted or DUPLICATED time column — a panel rather than a series — the spans are MEANINGLESS and nothing errors (silently wrong) ⇒ a hard stop; and the axis itself may hold no gaps. The check sorts with a radix order and looks for duplicates, rather than testing sortedness on text, which would depend on the LOCALE

THE RUNS DEPEND ON THE ROW ORDER — the patterns, the counts and the monotonicity do NOT: the tests pin an UNCHANGED mp_pattern result under a RANDOM ROW PERMUTATION. THE ONLY order-dependent field of mp_pattern is first_violating_row inside monotone, which is a ROW INDEX by definition

COLUMN-TYPE GATES — AN ESSENTIAL DIFFERENCE FROM #248: here NO moment is computed and NO coercion happens, so the unusual ATOMIC dtypes (a duration, a time-indexed value, a unit-carrying value, a labelled value) ARE ALLOWED, since the presence test is type-agnostic — whereas #248 BLOCKS them, because its moments would carry unknown units. What is blocked is EXACTLY the structures where the presence test does not return one flag per row: a matrix column and a frame column, which both return a MATRIX; a decomposed timestamp, internally a LIST of nine fields; a nested-list column, where the test looks inside each element rather than at the cell; and a complex column, which is not JSON-safe

POST-CHECKS AS MUTATION GUARDS (STRUCTURALLY impossible to trigger from a valid input; that is why they are SEPARATE functions that the tests call DIRECTLY): the sum of the pattern counts == nrow (the patterns PARTITION the rows); the complete cases derived from the patterns == a direct count; the sum of the run lengths per variable == its number of missing values (the completeness of the rle); rr+rm+mr+mm == nrow in EVERY cell

EDGE-CASE BEHAVIOUR (documented and tested, NEVER an error): NO missing values gives ONE pattern of all ones, n_patterns = 1, any_missing = False, monotone = True (empty sets are trivially nested), zero runs, and mm = 0 everywhere; an ALL-MISSING column gives ONE run with position='all', blank first and last observations, and does NOT break monotonicity; an ALL-MISSING dataset gives ONE pattern of all zeros and n_complete_cases = 0; a single row makes the per-column presence test return a VECTOR rather than a matrix (live-verified) ⇒ an explicit matrix fallback; and a single column makes mp_pairs return zero pairs with the CORRECT shape, rr and mm being 1x1

a df_handle AND NOT a matrix_handle at the node layer: coercing to a matrix WOULD DROP the NON-NUMERIC columns — that is, it would HIDE exactly the missing values the node exists to count, a silent data loss. These are TERMINAL nodes: nothing is registered and nothing chains onward

the conventional missing-data pattern and pair documentation — «1=observed, 0=missing»; «Rows and columns are sorted in increasing amounts of missing information»; «The last column and row contain row and column counts»; the pattern function draws by default; and for the pairs, rr is «both variables are observed», rm «row observed, column missing», mr the reverse, and mm «both variables are missing». cards.method: Battery of PARAMETRIC MEAN tests on CROSS-SECTION data: t-test (one sample / two samples Welch or Student pooled / paired) · one-way ANOVA (equal variances, a full ANOVA table) · the one-way Welch (1951) test WITHOUT the equal-variance assumption
cards.when: a FAST MEAN test on CROSS-SECTION data — countries, firms, households, survey respondents — BEFORE a heavy model is thrown at it: «does the sample's mean growth rate differ from 2%?» (tp_t_test one-sample) · «do euro and non-euro differ?» (two-sample; Welch = THE DEFAULT) · «did something change before/after the reform in the SAME units?» (paired) · «do THREE+ regions differ?» (tp_anova for the ANOVA table/eta^2; tp_welch when the variances are NOT equal or the n_i are very unequal)

interpretation_traps: NORMATIVE GATE 4 (the normative gate spec §3b) — CROSS-SECTION ONLY: AUTOCORRELATION INFLATES THE TYPE I ERROR, since it shrinks the variance estimator, giving spuriously significant p-values. EVERY exported function calls the SHARED cross-section gate (written ONCE in the shared gates module, and shared with #251 and #257; NEVER copied). Two branches, BOTH a hard stop: (a) an explicit rejection of any time-indexed input type; (b) a Ljung-Box whiteness precheck at lag = min(10, n/5), the DOCUMENTED default of the residual check (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, FPP 3rd ed. §5.4; the fitted-parameter count is 0, because the input is DATA rather than residuals) — a rejection at alpha stops the call. The message points EXPLICITLY at the HAC path, #35 in category 07. A CONSEQUENCE: the minimum n rises to 3, and for n < 5 the rule gives a lag below 1 ⇒ an explicit tested=False with decision='pass-untested' (NEVER a silent pass)

gate_alpha (default 0.05) — DECOUPLED FROM THE TEST'S alpha: alpha determines ONLY the reject/decision of the output; the level of the cross-section gate is ITS OWN argument (gate_alpha). WHY: the Ljung-Box precheck is a TEST OF SIZE gate_alpha, so BY CONSTRUCTION it blocks a small share of VALID i.i.d. input (a false block). LIVE-MEASURED (the engine, rnorm, 5000 replications): n=200 -> 1.6%/5.7%/10.1% and n=60 -> 2.3%/6.7%/10.8% for gate_alpha = 0.01/0.05/0.10. With the level tied, a «t-test at 10%» would raise the gate's false-block rate to ~10% WITHOUT any statistical justification

ordered (default True) — AN EXPLICIT DECLARATION OF ROW ORDER: the Ljung-Box statistic is A FUNCTION OF THE ORDER — LIVE-VERIFIED that THE SAME 60 numbers pass unsorted and are BLOCKED once sorted, which is exactly how a cross-section file arrives (countries alphabetically, firms by size); the mean tests themselves are PERMUTATION-INVARIANT. ordered=False means the user DECLARES that the rows carry no order, the whiteness branch is SKIPPED EXPLICITLY (branch='skipped-by-declaration', decision='pass-unordered', tested=False everywhere), and ALL the structural checks — non-finite values, n>=3, zero variance — REMAIN. The time-indexed-type rejection ALWAYS APPLIES (branch='class-rejected'). Supplying lb_lag TOGETHER WITH ordered=False is a hard stop: it is contradictory, and would otherwise be a silent no-op

WHERE EXACTLY THE GATE RUNS (statistically precise, not mechanical): one-sample -> on x; two-sample -> on x AND y SEPARATELY (each sample has its own mean and variance); paired -> ONLY on the DIFFERENCES d = x - y (autocorrelation that CANCELS in the difference does NOT inflate the paired test's Type I error — a gate on x/y would reject VALID analyses); anova/welch -> PER GROUP (a named list per level)

⚠️ A DOCUMENTED LIMIT OF THE GATE: in tp_anova/tp_welch the response column is split into groups BEFORE it reaches the gate, and `[` on a series returns an UNCLASSED numeric ⇒ the «time-series class» branch does NOT see a series column inside a data_frame. The SUBSTANTIVE branch (Ljung-Box PER GROUP) stays fully active. In tp_t_test the vector arrives AS IS ⇒ both branches are active (covered in the tests)

SILENTLY WRONG (THE MOST SERIOUS, live-verified the engine): with a NUMERIC or LOGICAL grouping column aov does NOT do an ANOVA — it does a LINEAR REGRESSION (Df = 1 instead of k-1) WITHOUT any error/warning; oneway_test likewise accepts numeric groups ⇒ a HARD GATE: the column must be a factor or character (convert with factor EXPLICITLY)

SILENTLY WRONG: the t-test on NON-NUMERIC input does NOT error — it emits ONLY warnings, that the argument is not numeric and that the coercion introduced blanks, and returns a blank; with the warnings muffled, as the call path does, it would pass COMPLETELY silently ⇒ a hard input-type gate

SILENTLY WRONG (INCONSISTENT BEHAVIOUR ACROSS TESTS): on an infinity or a NaN both the t-test AND the one-way Welch test do NOT error — they return a NaN statistic and a NaN p-value (the documentation: «no longer errors and returns a still not very useful result»); the ANOVA DOES error ⇒ ONE uniform policy, a hard stop everywhere

SILENTLY WRONG: the pooled Student test does NOT error when one sample has n = 1, whose variance is not even defined, and still returns a p-value ⇒ n >= 2 is checked PER SAMPLE explicitly; and a group of size 1 in an ANOVA leaves df_residual = 0, so the table comes back WITHOUT the «F value» and «Pr(>F)» columns and WITHOUT an error — hence an explicit shape check rather than a silent empty result

SILENTLY WRONG (ZERO VARIANCE — TWO DIFFERENT POLICIES): tp_welch (zero_var='any') weights by n_i/s_i², so ONE SINGLE constant group gives a NaN statistic and a NaN p-value, while with var_equal=True the F is infinite and p is 0; tp_anova (zero_var='all'): when ALL the groups are constant the residual sum of squares is around 1e-31 and the ANOVA returns an F near 1.83e+31 with p near 4.4e-93 — numerical garbage — or a NaN F when the whole of y is constant. The gate runs BEFORE the shared cross-section gate, so that the message stays test-specific

AN EXPLICIT MISSING-VALUE POLICY: the t-test and the ANOVA remove gaps SILENTLY — the documentation says missing values are silently removed, in pairs when the design is paired, and the ANOVA drops incomplete rows by default ⇒ the reported n is NOT the input n, and the design's BALANCE is altered. Here: na_action='fail' is the DEFAULT and a hard stop, while 'omit' removes EXPLICITLY and WITH a count — n_na is always in the output, dropping pairs in the paired design and ROWS in the ANOVA and Welch routes

NO formula ON THE SURFACE (a SECURITY rule): the one-way design has EXACTLY one term, so a formula adds no expressiveness — only attack surface. The user supplies COLUMN NAMES as strings, which are validated against the frame's columns and used ONLY as a lookup key; the model's formula is LITERALLY written in the code. There is ZERO path from a user string to a parse or an evaluation. The ANOVA table is returned with CANONICAL labels, term = ('group', 'Residuals'), plus the raw row names, so the frontend never sees the internal names

DETERMINISM (charter §5): NO RNG (closed-form t/F + Welch-Satterthwaite df) ⇒ NO seed. The level order is CANONICAL — sort(unique(g)), NOT order of appearance — and the factor is built EXPLICITLY in that order, so that the ANOVA table, the mean_by_group/sd_by_group and the Welch statistic do NOT depend on the row sorting (pinned in the tests: identical over 2 runs AND over shuffled rows)

POST-CHECKS (a DEFENSIVE «second net» — with the pre-gates active they are NOT triggered by any public call, which is why the tests exercise them directly): the result really is a test record, or an ANOVA fit; the statistic is finite and of length 1; the p-value is finite and within [0,1]; df_residual >= 1; and the ANOVA table carries ALL five columns and EXACTLY two rows

cards.method: Battery of NON-PARAMETRIC (rank-based) tests on CROSS-SECTION data: Wilcoxon signed rank (one sample / paired) & rank sum = Mann-Whitney (two independent) with an optional non-parametric CI + Hodges-Lehmann · Kruskal-Wallis (k >= 2 independent groups) · Friedman (unreplicated complete block design)
cards.when: the rank-based COUNTERPARTS of the parametric battery #250, when NORMALITY does NOT hold (#247) or the sample is very small: TWO independent groups of countries or firms -> tn_wilcox (rank sum, Mann-Whitney); BEFORE and AFTER on the SAME units -> tn_wilcox with paired=True, the signed rank of the differences; k >= 2 INDEPENDENT groups -> tn_kruskal, the non-parametric one-way ANOVA; k methods or treatments MEASURED ON THE SAME blocks (say 3 forecasting methods across 6 countries) -> tn_friedman, the non-parametric repeated-measures test
cards.when_not: TIME SERIES or time-dependent data — a HARD GATE (§3b normative gate 4); the HAC path is #35 (category 07); normality DOES hold and you want MORE power, an ANOVA table or an eta² -> #250; TWO CATEGORICAL variables, a contingency table with chi-squared, Fisher or Cramér's V -> #257; a normality DECISION -> #247, or #1 Jarque-Bera; a Friedman test WEIGHTED by the block range — NOT exposed, being a DIFFERENT test that would need its own card; an INCOMPLETE or REPLICATED block design (Friedman requires EXACTLY one observation per block-and-group pair); charts (the frontend, §5 — the node supplies rank_means, rank_sums and within_block_ranks as NUMBERS)

alternatives.criterion: ONE sample: signed rank; H0 = the distribution of x is SYMMETRIC about mu

alternatives.alt: tn_wilcox with a second sample, paired=False
alternatives.criterion: TWO INDEPENDENT samples: rank sum / Mann-Whitney; H0 = the distributions differ by a location shift equal to mu
PAIRED measurements on the SAME units, of EQUAL length; equivalent to the signed rank of the differences — the gaps are removed PAIRWISE

you want a MAGNITUDE, not only a p-value: a non-parametric CI + the Hodges-Lehmann estimator (pseudomedian or difference in location). ⚠️ At small n the ACHIEVED level differs from the requested one (conf_level_achieved) and the interval may come out infinite (conf_int_finite)
k >= 2 INDEPENDENT groups (list/matrix/data_frame): H0 = the same location parameter in every group; df = k-1

the k groups are NOT independent: they were ALL measured in EVERY block (country/unit); the ranks are computed WITHIN a block ⇒ the block effect is removed. WIDE (blocks x groups) or LONG (y + groups + blocks)
normality DOES hold: more power, an ANOVA table, eta^2 and confidence intervals for the means
NEITHER of the two variables is continuous — two CATEGORICAL answers per unit ⇒ a contingency table, not a comparison of medians
the data ARE time-dependent and inference MUST be done: HAC/clustered SE — NOT a bypass of the gate

interpretation_traps: NORMATIVE GATE 4 (the normative gate spec §3b) — CROSS-SECTION ONLY: all three tests presuppose INDEPENDENT observations, and autocorrelation INFLATES THE TYPE I ERROR ⇒ spuriously significant p-values. The rule is implemented ONCE in the SHARED cross-section gate (the shared gates module, shared with #250 and #257) and is CALLED here, NEVER copied: (a) an explicit rejection of any time-indexed input type and (b) a Ljung-Box whiteness precheck at lag = min(10, n/5), the DOCUMENTED default of the residual check (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, FPP 3rd ed. §5.4). The message points EXPLICITLY at the HAC path, #35 in category 07 (vcov_hac, vcov_cluster, vcov_panel). LIVE-VERIFIED: the Friedman routine accepts a time-indexed matrix WITHOUT COMPLAINT — ONLY the gate stops it. A CONSEQUENCE: the minimum n PER GROUP rises to 3, deliberately stricter than the underlying routine

gate_alpha (default 0.05) — THE LEVEL BELONGS EXCLUSIVELY TO THE GATE: the three non-parametric tests have no alpha of their own (no decision column), which is why the argument is called gate_alpha and NOT alpha. The precheck is a TEST OF SIZE gate_alpha ⇒ by construction it blocks a small share of VALID i.i.d. input; LIVE-MEASURED (the engine, rnorm, 5000 replications): n=200 -> 1.6%/5.7%/10.1%, n=60 -> 2.3%/6.7%/10.8% for 0.01/0.05/0.10

ordered (default True) — AN EXPLICIT DECLARATION OF ROW ORDER: the Ljung-Box statistic depends on the ORDER (live-verified: the same 60 numbers pass unsorted and are blocked once sorted) whereas the three rank tests are PERMUTATION-INVARIANT — Friedman with respect to the order of the BLOCKS. ordered=False omits the whiteness branch explicitly (branch='skipped-by-declaration', decision='pass-unordered'), while ALL the structural checks and the time-indexed-type rejection (branch='class-rejected') stay ACTIVE. Supplying lb_lag together with ordered=False is a hard stop

WHY NOTHING IS CONVERTED BEFORE THE GATE: the input's TYPE must survive INTACT as far as the gate, which is the SOLE owner of the rule rejecting time-indexed input; hence the gate comes LAST before the test, and the conversion happens AFTER. A KNOWN LIMITATION: when na_action='omit' or 'drop_blocks' REMOVES values, the subset loses its type ⇒ a time-indexed input WITH gaps, plus an explicit omit, is checked only by the whiteness branch; and in the LONG form of tn_friedman the gate sees the RESHAPED wide matrix, which is correct, since a stacked long vector is NOT a time series

AN INCONSISTENT documented policy FOR NON-FINITE VALUES (live-verified): the wilcox_test routine says of x/y «Non-finite (e.g., infinite or missing) values will be omitted» — but in the TWO-SAMPLE branch the Inf values are KEPT as «very large» (the release notes) ⇒ THE SAME Inf changes meaning depending on the branch. A hard gate: NO Inf/-Inf in any input

AN EXPLICIT MISSING-VALUE POLICY: the rank-sum and Kruskal-Wallis routines remove gaps SILENTLY (live-verified: a gap in one sample runs normally) and the Friedman routine removes WHOLE BLOCKS («if y contains NAs, corresponding blocks are removed») ⇒ silent data loss. Here: na_action='fail' is the DEFAULT hard stop, 'omit' covers the rank-sum and Kruskal-Wallis routes and works PAIRWISE in the paired design, and 'drop_blocks' covers Friedman — ALWAYS with a count (n_omitted, or n_blocks_dropped) and a check that at least two blocks remain

A DOCUMENTED CHANGE IN the reference >= 4.6.0 (A DEPARTURE FROM OLD KNOWLEDGE, live-verified): there is no longer a silent fallback to the normal approximation with the warning «cannot compute exact p-value with ties» — «If there are ties, exact inference is performed using the conditional/permutation distribution given the observed ranks, using an implementation of the Streitberg-Röhmel shift algorithm» (the wilcox_test routine; the reference NEWS 4.6.0, contributed by Torsten Hothorn). The node EXPOSES IT anyway as FIELDS (exact_used/normal_approximation/continuity_correction read FROM the method string; the release notes: «If exact computations are used, the result now has 'exact' in the method element») ⇒ if a future version falls back again, IT IS VISIBLE in the JSON instead of hidden

THE SAME SAMPLE, TWO V VALUES (a live finding in the engine): in the signed-rank test with ZERO differences the statistic is built in TWO WAYS — the exact route ranks the absolute differences with the zeros INSIDE and sums the ranks of the positive ones, while the asymptotic route DROPS the zeros FIRST. MEASURED on x = (0.6, 1, 1.4, 0.5, 1.3, 1.2, 1.3, 1.9) against mu = 1: V = 22 on the exact route against 17 on the asymptotic one. The node exposes zeroes_present and exact_used TOGETHER, and builds rank_means and rank_sums BY THE PATH THAT ACTUALLY RAN

A POST-CHECK OF THE IDENTITY between the chart data and the statistic (if it breaks, the frontend would draw NUMBERS OTHER than the p-value ⇒ a hard stop): for the two-sample rank sum, the rank sum of x minus n_x(n_x+1)/2 equals W, since the reference subtracts m(m+1)/2; for the signed rank, the positive rank sum equals V; for Kruskal-Wallis, the rank sums total N(N+1)/2; and for Friedman they total n_blocks * k(k+1)/2. The ranks are reproduced EXACTLY as the reference builds them — the same rank rounding, and the same shifted concatenation in the two-sample case

SILENTLY WRONG DEGENERACIES (live-verified, all hard-gated): ALL differences from mu zero -> the signed rank degenerates to V = 0, p = 1 WITHOUT an error; a completely constant pooled sample -> rank sum p = 1 / kruskal_test chi-squared = NaN & p = NaN WITHOUT an error (a 0/0 division in the tie correction); EVERY block with identical values -> friedman_test NaN/NaN WITHOUT an error

A SILENT DROP BY stats THAT IS AVOIDED STRUCTURALLY: kruskal_test documents «g is ignored with a warning if x is a list» ⇒ here the input is ALWAYS NORMALISED to a named list of groups (list/matrix/data_frame accepted), so that g can NEVER be ignored silently. Group names: NON-EMPTY and UNIQUE

FRIEDMAN IS AN UNREPLICATED COMPLETE BLOCK DESIGN («exactly one observation in y for each combination of levels of groups and blocks») ⇒ our own gates in the LONG form: NO REPLICATION and NO EMPTY block-and-group pair; at least 2 columns AND at least 2 rows, otherwise the routine throws a cryptic dimension error; and blank or empty labels are forbidden, since neither the groups nor the blocks may carry them. The ranks are WITHIN-BLOCK and are NOT compared across blocks

AN INTERVAL ONLY WHERE IT IS DOCUMENTED: conf_int and conf_level exist ONLY in tn_wilcox — the Kruskal-Wallis and Friedman routines document neither an interval nor an estimate, and nothing is invented. A live-verified trap: at small n the ACHIEVED level differs from the requested one (0.95 becomes 0.9609375) and the interval may come out (-Inf, Inf) WITHOUT a warning ⇒ conf_level, conf_level_achieved and conf_int_finite are exposed EXPLICITLY

digits_rank: when finite, the ranks are computed on the values rounded to that many significant digits — it stabilises tie detection when differences of order 1e-16 would hide them («For stability reasons, it may be advisable to use rounded data or to set the rank rounding to 7 significant digits»). The continuity correction is exposed ONLY as a boolean: its INTEGER form, 0 to 3 Edgeworth terms, is NOT recorded in the method string (live-verified: a value of 2 produces THE SAME «with continuity correction» text) ⇒ the output would be UNVERIFIABLE, and a numeric argument kind would turn True into 1, meaning «one Edgeworth term» — a silent change of meaning

DETERMINISM (charter §5): NO RNG path — no seed, no Monte-Carlo/permutation simulation. The exact distributions are closed-form (psignrank/pwilcox) or, under ties, the DETERMINISTIC Streitberg-Röhmel shift algorithm; identical over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (the wrapper AND the node path)
