cards.method: Ljung-Box and Box-Pierce portmanteau tests with Durbin-Watson
cards.when: the single most-used whiteness check in applied time series: are the residuals of a fitted model, or the series itself, free of remaining autocorrelation
cards.when_not: the data are cross-sectional; the residuals come from a model with lagged dependent variables, where Durbin-Watson is invalid and Breusch-Godfrey is required

alternatives.criterion: the regression contains lagged dependent variables
a quick first-order check on a static regression
you want the pattern rather than a single test

output_key_fields: statistic, p_value: per tested lag
df: degrees of freedom, reduced by the number of estimated model parameters
durbin_watson: the first-order statistic, around 2 under no autocorrelation
decision: whiteness verdict at alpha
interpretation_traps: when testing MODEL RESIDUALS the degrees of freedom must be reduced by the number of estimated ARMA parameters; failing to do so makes the test far too conservative
Durbin-Watson is INVALID with a lagged dependent variable -- it is biased toward 2 and will not detect autocorrelation that is there
the test has power against many alternatives and identifies none of them; a rejection says 'not white', not 'add one more lag'
sources: Ljung & Box 1978 (Biometrika 65:297-303)
Box & Pierce 1970 (JASA 65:1509)
Durbin & Watson 1951 (Biometrika 38:159)

cards.method: BDS test for independence and nonlinear structure
cards.when: asking whether what remains after a linear model is genuinely independent, or merely linearly uncorrelated with nonlinear structure left in it
cards.when_not: the sample is short -- the test needs several hundred observations to have a reliable null distribution

alternatives.criterion: you only want linear autocorrelation
you suspect nonlinear dependence such as ARCH or chaos
you specifically suspect conditional heteroskedasticity

output_key_fields: statistic, p_value: per embedding dimension and distance
embedding_dimension: the dimensions tested
epsilon: the distance thresholds used, in standard deviations
decision: independence verdict
interpretation_traps: the BDS statistic is sensitive to the choice of EPSILON and embedding dimension; report the grid, because a rejection at one setting is not a rejection
rejection means 'not independent and identically distributed' -- it does not identify the nonlinearity, and ARCH is the most common cause by far
applied to residuals of an estimated model the asymptotic distribution changes, and a bootstrap null is needed
sources: Brock, Dechert, Scheinkman & LeBaron 1996 (Econometric Reviews 15:197-235)
statsmodels.tsa.stattools.bds

cards.method: Long-run variance and HAC bandwidth selection
cards.when: estimating the spectral density at frequency zero -- the quantity every HAC standard error, unit-root test and cointegration statistic depends on
cards.when_not: the data are independent, where the long-run variance is just the variance

alternatives.criterion: the standard default
asymptotically optimal, though slower
strong persistence, where raw kernels are badly biased

output_key_fields: long_run_variance: the estimate
bandwidth: the truncation used and the rule that chose it
kernel: the kernel applied
prewhitened: whether an autoregressive filter was applied first
interpretation_traps: with strong persistence the kernel estimator is severely DOWNWARD biased, which makes HAC standard errors too small exactly when they matter most -- prewhitening is the standard remedy
the automatic bandwidth rules of Andrews and of Newey-West disagree materially and neither is right in general
a bandwidth exceeding the sample length silently truncates to the sample and reports a number that is not the estimator asked for
sources: Newey & West 1987 (Econometrica 55:703-708)
Andrews 1991 (Econometrica 59:817-858)
Andrews & Monahan 1992 (Econometrica 60:953)
arch

cards.method: SADF and GSADF explosive-bubble tests with date stamping
cards.when: testing for explosive rather than merely non-stationary behaviour, and dating when the episodes began and ended
cards.when_not: the series has one break rather than a bubble; the sample is too short for the recursive windows to be estimated

alternatives.criterion: the alternative is stationarity, not explosiveness
a single suspected bubble episode
several episodes, which SADF has low power against

output_key_fields: sadf, gsadf: the supremum statistics
critical_values: simulated critical values, which are not tabulated in general
episodes: dated start and end of each explosive period
bsadf: the backward-supremum sequence used for dating
interpretation_traps: critical values must be SIMULATED for the specific sample size and window; using values from a paper with a different sample is simply wrong
SADF has low power when there are multiple bubbles, because a later episode contaminates the recursive windows -- that is what GSADF is for
the minimum window length is a tuning choice that determines how short an episode can be detected and moves the dating
sources: Phillips, Wu & Yu 2011 (International Economic Review 52:201-226)
Phillips, Shi & Yu 2015 (International Economic Review 56:1043)

cards.method: Panel cross-sectional dependence: Pesaran CD, LM and scaled LM
cards.when: testing whether panel units share common shocks, which invalidates every standard error that assumes independence across units
cards.when_not: the panel has a single unit; the cross-section is so large relative to time that the pairwise correlations cannot be estimated

alternatives.criterion: large N and small T, the usual macro panel
small N and large T
moderate N, correcting the LM size distortion

output_key_fields: statistic, p_value: the dependence test
average_correlation: mean absolute pairwise residual correlation
test: which variant was applied and why it suits the panel dimensions
decision: independence verdict
interpretation_traps: the LM test is badly OVERSIZED when N is large relative to T -- it rejects almost always, which is why Pesaran's CD exists
rejection means standard errors assuming cross-sectional independence are wrong; Driscoll-Kraay or common-factor methods are the response
the average absolute correlation is the economically informative number; the test statistic alone conflates size and strength
sources: Pesaran 2004/2021 (Empirical Economics 60:13-50)
Breusch & Pagan 1980 (Review of Economic Studies 47:239)

cards.method: Multicollinearity: variance inflation, tolerance and Belsley condition indices
cards.when: diagnosing whether the regressors are so nearly collinear that individual coefficients are unidentified in practice, even though the fit is fine
cards.when_not: there is a single regressor; the model is used only for prediction, where collinearity does not hurt

alternatives.criterion: a per-regressor screen
you want to know WHICH regressors are involved
you accept the collinearity and want stable coefficients

output_key_fields: vif, tolerance: per regressor
condition_index: per eigenvalue, largest being the condition number
variance_decomposition: which regressors load on each near-dependency
flagged: regressors above the chosen thresholds
interpretation_traps: a VIF threshold of 10 is a CONVENTION, not a result -- collinearity is a matter of degree and the threshold has no theoretical basis
VIFs identify that collinearity exists but not which regressors are collinear WITH WHICH; only the variance decomposition does that
collinearity does not bias coefficients or harm prediction; it inflates standard errors, and treating it as a bias problem leads to wrong fixes
sources: Belsley, Kuh & Welsch 1980, Regression Diagnostics
statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence

cards.method: Automatic seasonal-period detection and differencing orders
cards.when: deciding the seasonal period and the differencing orders before a model is fitted, by a stated rule rather than by inspection
cards.when_not: the period is known from the data's frequency; the series is too short for the tests to be reliable

alternatives.criterion: the period is unknown or multiple
you want d chosen by a test
theory or convention fixes the orders

output_key_fields: period: the detected seasonal period or periods
d, D: the selected non-seasonal and seasonal differencing orders
test_path: the sequence of tests and their outcomes, so the choice is auditable
seasonal_strength: the strength measure behind the period detection
interpretation_traps: OVER-DIFFERENCING is as damaging as under-differencing: it induces a non-invertible moving-average unit root that no estimator handles well
seasonal differencing is a strong assumption; a deterministic seasonal pattern is better handled with dummies or harmonics
the automatic rules differ between implementations and a series can get d=1 from one and d=0 from another
sources: Hyndman & Khandakar 2008 (Journal of Statistical Software 27:1-22)
Wang, Smith & Hyndman 2006 (Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 13:335)
statsforecast

cards.method: Stability without a known break date: Nyblom-Hansen, Andrews-Ploberger and Quandt-Andrews
cards.when: testing for parameter instability when you do not know, and must not pretend to know, when the break happened
cards.when_not: the break date is known from an event (use a Chow test); the sample is too short for the trimmed search range to contain anything

alternatives.criterion: the break date is known independently
one unknown break
power against a broader class of instability

output_key_fields: statistic: the supremum, average or exponential statistic
break_date: the argmax date, where the supremum test is used
critical_values: from the non-standard distribution these tests require
trimming: the search range, which determines what could be found
interpretation_traps: the null distribution is NON-STANDARD -- these are not chi-squared tests, and using conventional critical values grossly over-rejects
the estimated break date has wide sampling uncertainty; reporting it as a point without an interval overstates precision
TRIMMING excludes the ends of the sample from the search, so a break in the first or last 15% cannot be found at all
sources: Andrews 1993 (Econometrica 61:821-856)
Andrews & Ploberger 1994 (Econometrica 62:1383)
Nyblom 1989 (JASA 84:223)
statsmodels

cards.method: Long memory: Hurst exponent, rescaled range, detrended fluctuation and variance ratio
cards.when: distinguishing genuine long-range dependence from a short-memory process with a trend or a break, which mimic it closely
cards.when_not: the series is plainly short memory; the sample is too short for the scaling exponent to be estimated over enough scales

alternatives.criterion: the classic estimator, though biased by short memory
the series is non-stationary or trending
the question is a random walk against mean reversion

output_key_fields: hurst: the estimated exponent, 0.5 under independence
method: which estimator produced it
scaling_range: the scales the exponent was fitted over
variance_ratio, p_value: the random-walk test where requested
interpretation_traps: STRUCTURAL BREAKS AND TRENDS MIMIC LONG MEMORY -- an exponent above 0.5 is not evidence of long memory until breaks have been excluded
the estimate depends strongly on the range of scales fitted; reporting the exponent without the scaling range is uninformative
the rescaled-range estimator is biased upward in small samples even for independent data
sources: Hurst 1951 (Transactions of the American Society of Civil Engineers 116:770)
Peng et al. 1994 (Physical Review E 49:1685)
Lo & MacKinlay 1988 (Review of Financial Studies 1:41-66)
nolds

cards.method: Unsupervised anomaly detection: isolation forest, local outlier factor and one-class SVM
cards.when: flagging observations that do not belong, in a multivariate setting where univariate outlier rules see nothing
cards.when_not: the outliers are defined by a known rule; the data are a time series where the anomaly is contextual and needs a temporal model

alternatives.criterion: many observations, mixed feature types
density varies across the space
a tight boundary around a well-defined normal region

output_key_fields: scores: the anomaly score per observation
flagged: observations above the threshold
contamination: the assumed anomaly rate, which sets the threshold
feature_contributions: what drove each flag, where the method provides it
interpretation_traps: the CONTAMINATION parameter effectively sets how many anomalies you find -- it is an assumption, not a discovery, and the flagged count follows it almost mechanically
these methods are unsupervised: 'anomalous' means unusual, not wrong, and the two are frequently different things
distance-based detectors degrade badly in high dimensions as all points become equidistant
sources: Liu, Ting & Zhou 2008, Isolation forest (ICDM 2008:413-422)
Breunig, Kriegel, Ng & Sander 2000 (SIGMOD Record 29:93)

cards.method: Time-series feature extraction at scale
cards.when: turning many series into a comparable feature matrix, for clustering, screening or as inputs to a global model
cards.when_not: you have one series and want to understand it, where targeted diagnostics beat a large undirected feature set

alternatives.criterion: one series and a specific question
many series, and you want a comparable matrix
you want a compact, interpretable set

output_key_fields: features: the extracted feature matrix
selected: features surviving the relevance filter, where one is applied
n_features: how many were computed and how many survived
missing_features: features undefined for some series and why
interpretation_traps: computing hundreds of features and selecting on the outcome is MULTIPLE TESTING; the relevance filter's p-values must be adjusted or the selection is spurious
many features are undefined for short or constant series and return missing values that propagate silently into downstream models
features are not scale invariant unless the series are normalised first, so cross-series comparison needs an explicit decision
sources: Christ, Braun, Neuffer & Kempa-Liehr 2018 (Neurocomputing 307:72-77)
Fulcher & Jones 2017 (Cell Systems 5:527)
tsfresh

cards.method: Distance correlation and general independence tests
cards.when: detecting dependence of any form, not just linear -- a screen that will not miss a relationship because it is not monotone
cards.when_not: you specifically want a linear measure; the sample is large enough that the permutation null is prohibitive

alternatives.criterion: the relationship is linear
any dependence, no functional form assumed
you want an information-theoretic measure

output_key_fields: dcor: distance correlation, zero if and only if independent
statistic, p_value: the independence test
partial_dcor: partialling out a third set, where supplied
n_permutations: the null the p-value came from
interpretation_traps: distance correlation is ZERO IF AND ONLY IF INDEPENDENT, which Pearson is not -- that is the whole reason to use it
it detects dependence without characterising it; a high value says look at the scatter, not what the relationship is
the permutation null is O(n squared) per replication and becomes prohibitive well before the data are large
sources: Szekely, Rizzo & Bakirov 2007 (Annals of Statistics 35:2769-2794)
Szekely & Rizzo 2014 (Annals of Statistics 42:2382)

cards.method: Entropy diagnostics: sample, permutation, approximate and spectral entropy
cards.when: measuring how predictable or complex a series is, as a model-free screen before deciding what to fit
cards.when_not: the series is very short, where every entropy estimator is badly biased; you need a specific dependence test rather than a complexity summary

alternatives.criterion: robust, ordinal, fast
regularity of amplitude patterns
how concentrated the spectrum is

output_key_fields: entropy: the estimated value per measure
normalised: scaled to the unit interval where the measure permits
parameters: embedding dimension and tolerance, which drive the answer
forecastability: one minus normalised spectral entropy, a rough predictability index
interpretation_traps: sample and approximate entropy depend strongly on the TOLERANCE and embedding dimension; values computed with different settings are not comparable
approximate entropy is biased by self-matching, which is exactly what sample entropy was introduced to remove
entropy is not stationary-invariant: a trend lowers apparent complexity and can be mistaken for structure
sources: Richman & Moorman 2000 (American Journal of Physiology 278:H2039-H2049)
Bandt & Pompe 2002 (Physical Review Letters 88:174102)
antropy

cards.method: Recurrence quantification analysis
cards.when: detecting deterministic structure, regime changes and intermittency by quantifying when a system revisits earlier states
cards.when_not: the series is short or heavily noise dominated, where the recurrence plot shows nothing but speckle

alternatives.criterion: you suspect deterministic or regime structure
you want a scalar complexity summary
you specifically want dated regime changes

output_key_fields: recurrence_rate: density of recurrences
determinism: share of recurrences on diagonal lines
laminarity, trapping_time: vertical-structure measures indicating intermittency
entropy: diagonal-line-length entropy
interpretation_traps: the RECURRENCE THRESHOLD determines everything; a common convention fixes the recurrence rate rather than the distance, and the two give different pictures
embedding parameters must be chosen before analysis -- mutual information for the delay, false nearest neighbours for the dimension -- and defaults are rarely right
high determinism is not proof of a deterministic system; coloured noise produces it too
sources: Marwan, Romano, Thiel & Kurths 2007 (Physics Reports 438:237-329)
Webber & Zbilut 1994 (Journal of Applied Physiology 76:965)
PyRQA

cards.method: Benford digit tests
cards.when: screening reported figures for the digit pattern naturally occurring data usually follow, as a first check for fabrication or rounding
cards.when_not: the data are bounded, assigned or generated by a process with no reason to follow the law -- most identifiers, ages and scores

alternatives.criterion: the standard screen
more power, needs more observations
targeting rounding rather than fabrication

output_key_fields: observed, expected: digit frequencies against the law
chi_square, mad, p_value: conformity statistics
conformity: the conventional verdict band the MAD falls in
n_observations: the count, which drives whether any of this is meaningful
interpretation_traps: BENFORD DOES NOT APPLY to every dataset -- it needs several orders of magnitude and no assignment rule; applying it to bounded data manufactures a failure
a rejection is a screening flag, not evidence of fraud; rounding, thresholds and unit changes all produce it
the chi-squared test rejects almost any large sample; the mean absolute deviation bands are what practitioners actually read
sources: Benford 1938 (Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 78:551)
Nigrini 2012, Benford's Law: Applications for Forensic Accounting, Auditing and Fraud Detection
